segments.text: That's the log-normal distribution.

segments.text: Here's the definition, in simple words.
segments.caption: Here's the definition, in simple words.

segments.text: A log-normal distribution has only positive values, and it's skewed to the right.
segments.caption: A log-normal distribution has only positive values, and it's skewed to the right.

segments.text: But take the log of every value, and you get a normal bell curve.
segments.caption: But take the log of every value, and you get a normal bell curve.

segments.text: That's the name: its logs are normal.

segments.text: So what's a log? Here's the easy way to think about it.
segments.caption: So what's a log? Here's the easy way to think about it.

segments.text: A log counts the zeros. The log of ten is one. The log of a hundred is two. The log of a thousand is three.
segments.caption: A log counts the zeros. The log of 10 is 1. The log of 100 is 2. The log of 1,000 is 3.

segments.text: So on a log scale, each step means times ten.
segments.caption: So on a log scale, each step means times ten.

segments.text: The same prices form a symmetric bell. That's log-normal.

segments.text: Why does this happen? Because prices grow by percentages.

segments.text: A ten percent rise adds two lakh to a twenty lakh flat, but twenty lakh to a two crore villa.

segments.text: Growth that multiplies, instead of adding, stretches the big values out. That makes the long tail.

segments.text: You'll see log-normal data everywhere: incomes, house prices, the time to finish a task, and stock prices.
